name: GenieDB
tagline: Defunct geo-distributed MySQL storage engine that later became a MySQL DBaaS (c. 2008–2015).
description: GenieDB sold technology for running MySQL across multiple datacenters or cloud regions. It started as a MySQL storage engine that replicated tables between geographically distant sites with automatic conflict handling and self-healing after outages, pitched at WordPress, Drupal and other CMS sites that wanted to survive a region failure without moving to NoSQL. Around 2014 it repositioned as a hosted MySQL database-as-a-service with a web console and multi-cloud placement. The company stopped operating around 2015 and its domain is now parked. Today the same need is met by Galera-based clusters, Aurora Global Database, PlanetScale or TiDB.
statusNote: Company ceased operations around 2015; geniedb.com is parked. Use Galera Cluster, Aurora or PlanetScale for multi-site MySQL.

pricing.notes: Historically sold as a storage engine and later as a hosted MySQL service.

scale.notes: Focused on replicating MySQL data between regions rather than sharding it.

strengths: Multi-region MySQL without changing the application
Installed like any other MySQL storage engine
Aimed squarely at CMS sites such as WordPress and Drupal
weaknesses: Cross-region replication traded away strict consistency
useCases: Historical example of geo-replicated MySQL storage engines
Background when evaluating multi-region MySQL options
